question: Swami Vivekanand’s organisation _________ stressed the ideal of salvation through social service and selfless action.
solution:
The correct answer is __Ramakrishna Mission__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ramakrishna Mission (RKM) is a Hindu religious and spiritual organization that forms the core of a worldwide spiritual movement known as the Ramakrishna Movement or the Vedanta Movement.
 
• Swami Vivekananda established the Ramakrishna Mission to stress the ideals of salvation through social service and selfless action.
 
• The mission is named after and inspired by the Indian saint Ramakrishna Paramahamsa and founded by Ramakrishna's chief disciple Swami Vivekananda on 1 May 1897.
 
• The mission bases its work on the principles of karma yoga, the principle of selfless work done with a dedication to God.
 
• The Ramakrishna Mission is centered around the world and publishes many important Hindu texts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• After the break-up and disintegration of the **Brahmo Samaj**, the** Sadharan Brahmo Samaj** was founded in 1878 by **Anand Mohan Bose, Ravindra Nath Tagore's father Devendra Nath** **Tagore **was actively associated with this society. The ordinary Brahmo Samaj believed that rebirth after death is a natural action.
 
• The Veda Samaj​:
 
 
• Veda Samaj was established by Keshab Chandra Sen and K. Sridharalu Naidu when the former visited Madras in 1864.
 
 
 
• In 1923, B.R Ambedkar__ set up the 'Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha' (Outcastes Welfare Association), which was devoted to spreading education and culture amongst the downtrodden, improving the economic status and raising matters concerning their problems in the proper forums to focus attention on them and finding solutions to the same.
 
 
• The problems of the downtrodden were centuries old and difficult to overcome.
 
• Their entry into temples was forbidden.
 
• They could not draw water from public wells and ponds.
 
• Their admission in schools was prohibited.
